hero.titleLine1: Turn an idea into a project,
hero.titleLine2: then find teammates who show up
hero.body: Write down an idea. The AI only asks questions and never thinks for you, so you work out what to build and who is missing. Then it suggests just a few people from your school or circle, each with why they fit and what the risk is.

pain.title: Finding people is easy. Finding reliable ones isn't.

items.title: No one outside your field
items.body: A project needs engineering, design and business, but your network stops at your own major. Posting and group chats come down to luck.

items.title: Interested, but not committed
items.body: Saying you're interested costs nothing. People vanishing halfway through is the most common way small teams fail.

items.title: Lots of information, hard to decide
items.body: Even with profiles and chat logs in front of you, it's hard to tell who fits and who will follow through.

how.title: From a one-line idea to a team ready to start

steps.title: The AI asks, you think
steps.body: Three key questions per round, answered in your own words. The AI points out gaps but doesn't think for you.

steps.title: Shape it into a project
steps.body: Get a vision, blockers, a two-week plan and role cards for who's missing, plus a kickoff prompt you can hand to other AI tools.

steps.title: A few good matches
steps.body: Only a handful of people from your school or circle, each with why they fit and the main risk.

demo.title: Three steps from idea to teammate
demo.scoreNote: Each with a reason and a risk

preview.title: Every suggestion explains why, and what could go wrong
preview.body: No endless feed. You get a few people or projects at a time, each flagged with the one risk that matters most, such as "can only give 4 hours a week, below the 6 the role needs". You decide faster instead of drowning in information.

trust.title: Turn "interested" into "committed"
trust.body: Applications state how many hours a week you can give, and you can only have 3 open at once. Every new member starts with a two-week trial. What you finish is recorded and becomes your track record for the next team.
trust.cardsDescription: Scroll to see how we cut down on people who agree to join and then vanish.
items: Core ideas only for accepted members

items.question: How is this different from posting in a group chat?
items.answer: A post only helps you find people. We help you find reliable ones: the AI breaks your needs into roles, every suggestion comes with a reason and a risk, applicants commit hours, and there's a trial period.

items.question: Does the AI decide for me?
items.answer: No. The AI only asks questions and gathers evidence; who to pick and what to do is up to you. It suggests just a few people at a time so you're never buried.

items.question: Could someone take my idea?
items.answer: Public posts only show the direction and the roles you need. The core idea is visible only to accepted applicants, and every edit is timestamped.

items.question: Where can I use it?
items.answer: During the beta we're piloting with a few schools and research groups. Sign up with your school email to join.

final.title: Your next great project may be one teammate away
final.body: Spend five minutes thinking your idea through. Matching does the rest.
